exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return {x}
    out = {x, f"{v:g}"}
    if v == int(v):
        out.add(str(int(v)))
    return out


def read_register(path):
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xlsm")):
        try:
            import openpyxl
        except ImportError:
            sys.exit("--register on .xlsx needs openpyxl; export the sheet to CSV")
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)
        rows = []
        for ws in wb.worksheets:
            rows += [["" if c is None else str(c) for c in r] for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]
        return rows
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig", errors="replace") as fh:
        return list(csv.reader(fh))


def register_check(path, limit):
    """Checks a requirement/constraint register against the indexed corpus. First output line is machine-readable."""
    rows = [r for r in read_register(path) if any(str(c).strip() for c in r)]
    if len(rows) < 2:
        print("REGISTER rows=0")
        print("register is empty")
        return 1
    head = [str(c).strip() for c in rows[0]]
    src = [i for i, h in enumerate(head) if SRC_COL.search(h)]
    val = [i for i, h in enumerate(head) if VAL_COL.search(h) and i not in src]
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    docs = {}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in fns:
            if fn.endswith(".txt"):
                full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
                docs[os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]] = full
    cache = {}

    def text_of(d):
        if d not in cache:
            cache[d] = re.sub(r"(?<=\d),(?=\d{3})", "", read_text(docs[d]))
        return cache[d]

    def match_docs(cell):
        toks = [t for t in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{2,}", cell) if not re.fullmatch(r"[\d.]+", t)]
        hits = []
        for d in docs:
            name = os.path.basename(d).lower()
            score = sum(1 for t in toks if t.lower() in name)
            if score:
                hits.append((score, d))
        hits.sort(reverse=True)
        return [d for s, d in hits if s == hits[0][0]] if hits else []

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1.
The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2.
Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3.
Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4.
Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.

5.
The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.

Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.

§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
Holiday | Observed Date
Memorial Day | 05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day | 06/19/2025
Independence Day | 07/04/2025


(d)Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and

The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:
•
the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
•
for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;


--- page 3 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office
Page 3
•
for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;
•
the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;
•
correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.
End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.

for x in allmin: print(x)

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW SCREEN DETERMINATION
To:      Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
From:   Priya Ranganathan, Interconnection Studies
Date:   06/25/2025
Subject: Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW, Feeder ALN-214) — Supplemental Review Screen Determination
1. Project
The application was routed to supplemental review following failure of an initial fast-track screen. This memo records the disposition of the 100%-of-minimum-load screen applied under SRP-3 Rev 3.
2. Screen applied
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar, per §4 of SRP-3 (Rev 3, effective 02/10/2025). Under this screen, the requested DER capacity is compared against the minimum load observed on the subject feeder from AMI interval data.
3. Analysis
Reviewed AMI interval load data for Feeder ALN-214 from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse and identified a minimum feeder load of 1.1 MW. The value was drawn from the feeder AMI record available on file for ALN-214. No intervals were excluded for known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching during the period reviewed.
4. Comparison
1.8 MW requested exceeds 1.1 MW minimum feeder load — screen FAILED.
5. Recommendation
Study Agreement required prior to advancement. The application should not proceed on the supplemental-review track. A Study Agreement should be offered to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC, with the scope covering the technical conditions that gave rise to the failed screen on Feeder ALN-214.
6. Disposition
Return supplemental review file to Interconnection Studies queue with a failed-screen flag on Feeder ALN-214.
Notify the applicant of the screen result and forward the Study Agreement package.
Hold advancement of PXA record for Bramwick Commons Solar until Study Agreement is executed.

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities

Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com
1. Purpose
This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
4. Interim Netted Figure
Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
5. Recommendation
Distribution Planning recommends the following:
Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

---
name: professional-memo
description: How to write an engineering memo, letter, reply, review response or technical note for a named recipient, written for an expert reader - answer first, basis from the record, every issue with owner and timing, exact scope, signature block, and a correct DOCX file. Use whenever the deliverable is a memo, letter, reply, response, review, disposition or note.
---

# Professional engineering memo

## Before writing
- Identify: who asked, who will act on the memo, the decision they must take, the "as of" date of the record, and any
  dates in the request (target date, deadline). Note what the request says is OUT of scope and leave it out.
- Gather the record: correspondence (emails, letters, RFIs), applications, studies, test reports, standards, contracts,
  tracking data in project applications. Build a dated timeline of relevant events in `/tmp/ahpele/timeline.md`.
- For each potential issue, find the exact source (document, section, date) and what it requires.
- For go/no-go questions (approve, issue, energise, accept, pay), do not stop at the first favourable reading. Build a checklist of every condition that applies
  (agreements, studies, permits, tests, payments, insurance, notices, deadlines, sign-offs, open correspondence) and
  check each one against the record as of the stated date. Only conclude that nothing blocks the decision after every
  condition has been checked and cited.

## Structure
1. Header: To / From / Date (use the record's "as of" date unless told otherwise) / Subject / project identifiers.
2. **Answer first**: one or two sentences that directly answer the question (yes / no / not yet, by which date), with
   the decisive reason.
3. **Basis**: the facts and requirements the answer rests on, each cited to the record (document, section, date).
4. **Open items** (one per issue): what it is; what requirement it rests on (cite it); what has to be done; who must do
   it (name the party or role, including the customer/applicant when it is theirs); whether it can be done before the
   target date and why; consequence if not.
5. Items reviewed and found acceptable, briefly, so the reader knows they were checked.
6. Scope statement: what this memo does not cover, exactly as the request defines it.
7. Recommendation / next steps with dates.
8. Signature block for the reviewing engineer if the request asks for one (name/title placeholders only where the
   request leaves the signer unnamed; never invent credentials).

## Determinations the reader can check
- Make a list of every question and request in the instruction (asks.md) and answer each one in its own labelled place.
- Each answer states the specific fact and the conclusion in one or two plain sentences: "<thing> is / is not <state>,
  because <fact with value and unit> (<document, section/sheet, date>)". Then give the working.
- When the record does not let you decide a question, say exactly what is missing, who must provide it and what the
  decision is meanwhile.
- Commit to one disposition per question, as engineering requests usually ask.
- Name the cause, not only the symptom: when something fails or is non-conforming, state why (which input, assumption,
  revision or condition) and what has to change.

## Scope, states and length
- Keep a scope ledger: what the request asks, what it excludes, what is under someone else's review. Items under separate
  review are mentioned, not decided; items that bear on the answer stay in even if raised elsewhere.
- Check the answer in every operating state or stage the request covers (before / during / after an event, normal and
  abnormal), not only the steady case.
- Length and precision follow the reader: a decision memo is usually 1-3 pages plus attachments; report numbers to the
  precision of the data (not six decimals); match tone and distribution to an internal or external recipient.

## Quality rules
- Be specific: dates, amounts, ratings, section numbers, document titles. No vague hedging.
- Distinguish facts from the record, requirements, and your engineering judgement.
- Check arithmetic and dates (business days, notice periods, expiry dates) with a script.
- Do not contradict yourself between the answer and the open items.
- Claim only actions that were actually taken (a request "has been sent" only if you sent it, with its record);
  otherwise write what should be done and by whom. Each follow-up becomes its own tracked item (ticket, task,
  register line with owner and date), not only a sentence inside a closed record.
- External letters carry no internal matters (internal case numbers, staff deliberations, other customers'
  correspondence, internal directives); keep those in the internal memo.
- Before netting a figure against a published baseline (capacity, budget, allowance), check what that baseline
  already includes and excludes, and say so.

## Producing the file
- Write DOCX with python-docx when available (`import docx`); otherwise use the word processing MCP tool if the task
  provides one, or build the file with LibreOffice (`soffice --headless --convert-to docx file.md` or `.html`).
- Use real headings and tables, not Markdown symbols inside the Word text.

---
name: engineering-deliverables
description: Method for engineering design and calculation packages graded against requirements - document precedence, superseded documents, requirement/constraint registers, hard-constraint checks, unit discipline, optimisation within constraints, and schema-exact deliverable files (CSV, JSON, XLSX, ZIP, IFC). Use for any task that asks for calculations, a design, a plan, a schedule, a register or a structured submission.
---

# Engineering deliverables

## 1. Know exactly what is graded
- Copy every deliverable requirement from the instruction into `/tmp/ahpele/checklist.md`: path, file name, format,
  required columns/keys/tokens (exact spelling), units, row granularity ("one row per X and Y"), and any scoring rule.
- The instruction is a data contract. Use its column names, token vocabularies and IDs verbatim. Extra columns are
  usually harmless; missing or renamed ones are not.
- If the instruction states how the work is scored (e.g. hard constraints gate the score, cost objective, recall of a
  register), let that decide where effort goes: never trade a hard constraint for objective value.

## 2. Document precedence and status
- Read the governing specification first: it usually lists which standards, revisions and documents apply.
- Typical precedence (unless the project documents say otherwise): addenda / RFI responses / site instructions issued
  later > specification > drawings > schedules > vendor data > reference standards. Later dated responses override
  earlier ones on the same point.
- A document marked superseded, cancelled, withdrawn, void or draft, or an older revision of a document that exists in
  a newer revision, is not an authority. Do not cite it, do not take values from it. Record in your narrative that you
  saw it and why you set it aside.
- Words like "cancelled" inside a document's text often describe another document. Check before discarding.

## 3. Requirements table and register
- Before designing, list every hard requirement with: id, document, clause/table, requirement, limit value, unit, what
  it binds (which items). Save as `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv`.
- Hard requirements include: safety and code limits, permit/authorisation limits (discharge, noise, setbacks),
  capacities (power, flow, head, load), resource caps (equipment, crews, water, budget), milestones and deadlines.
- If a register is a deliverable, build it from this table. Cite real project documents and clauses, not the brief.
  Cite only documents that are in force.

## 4. Calculations
- Work in one unit system internally; convert at the boundary. Keep inputs, intermediate results and units in a script
  (`/tmp/ahpele/calc.py`) so numbers can be recomputed after every change.
- Take every input from a document you can cite; write assumptions down where the documents leave a choice.
- Cross-check: totals equal sums of parts, the same quantity has the same value in every file, schedules respect
  durations and predecessors, quantities respect the caps.

## 5. Build early, then improve
- Produce a complete first version of every deliverable early with conservative choices that satisfy all hard
  requirements, even if it is not optimal. An incomplete or missing file scores nothing.
- Never write placeholders (TBD, NaN, "to be determined") in a numeric field. If a value is genuinely not applicable,
  use the not-applicable convention the instruction allows (often blank, N/A or NONE).

## 6. Verify with code
- Write `/tmp/ahpele/check.py` that loads your deliverable files exactly as written and tests every requirement row and
  every checklist item (columns, tokens, units, ranges, cross-file consistency). Run it after every change.
- Run the format checker: `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <deliverable paths>`.
- For CAD/BIM outputs, re-open the file with the standard library you wrote it with and check the entities, property
  sets and attributes the instruction names.
- IFC written by hand (no BIM library): generate it with a small script, not by typing STEP lines. Copy each entity
  pattern from the example file the task provides (or from the schema), keep every attribute in order (use `$` for an
  unset one; an IfcBuildingStorey has 10 attributes, an IfcPropertySet 5, an IfcRelDefinesByProperties 6), write every REAL
  with a decimal point (`20.` or `20.0`, never `20` and never `4.5.`; coordinates, directions, depths, elevations), and double apostrophes inside strings. Run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_ifc.py <file>` until it reports 0 errors, and compare its structure printout
  (storeys and elevations, property sets, footprints, heights) with what the contract requires. One unreadable
  entity can make the whole file unreadable.
- Placed or routed 3D models (coordination models, MEP routing, layouts): verify the FILE, not your script's variables.
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_clash.py <file.ifc> --point <entry x,y,z>` re-reads it with ifcopenshell's geometry
  engine in world coordinates and lists clashing pairs, element classes stacked at one spot, broken runs and the
  distance from each run to the entry point. Coordinates in `IfcCartesianPoint` are in the project length unit (a
  millimetre project takes millimetres); library helpers such as `ifcopenshell.api` placement calls take SI metres and
  convert for you, so do not divide by 1000 by hand as well. Iterate until 0 clashes and one network per service.

## 7. Optimise last
- Only after all hard checks pass: improve the objective (cost, performance) with a systematic search (enumerate
  options, or scipy.optimize when available), re-running the checks for every candidate. Keep the best feasible plan
  on disk at all times.

--- page 1 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW PROCEDURE
Doc no.
Rev
Effective date
Owner
SRP-3
Rev 3
02/10/2025
Alleniom Standards Engineering
Supersedes: SRP-3 Rev 2 (effective 07/22/2022)
Classification: Technical Standard — Distributed Energy Resource Interconnection
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Planning; Standards Engineering;
Regulatory Affairs
§1   Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.
§2   Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a)  all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b)  all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a)  sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b)  capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c)  domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.
§3   Screens


--- page 2 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 2
Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.
Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.
Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.
Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
fall below the values specified in DPS-07.
Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.
Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
place, the application shall be routed to study.
Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.
§4   100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
the site to pass the screen.
The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
data-window length in the supplemental review memo.
The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.
Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
file.
§5   Data sources
The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:


--- page 3 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 3
(a)  Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
minimum-load determination described in §4.
(b)  Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.
(c)  DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
A.
(d)  Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.
(e)  Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).
Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
reason for the substitution.
§6   Documentation
The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:
(a)  application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;
(b)  the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;
(c)  for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;
(d)  the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
applicant with specified deficiency;
(e)  reviewer signature and date; and
(f)  the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.
The memo shall be filed to the interconnection application record within five (5) business days of screen
completion. Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the
superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover.

This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
• classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);

• treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).

this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.
§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
• IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.

protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.
• TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.
• CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL

DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.
Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer

§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.


--- page 4 ---
DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
Page 4
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
certification and Control Narrative are always required.

a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5

Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
