§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. --- page 1 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
DISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD
Doc no.
Rev
Date
Owner
DPS-07
Rev 2
09/15/2023
Alleniom Standards Engineering
Effective date: 09/15/2023
Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)
Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering
1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


--- page 2 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 2
•
Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
•
Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.


--- page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the


--- page 4 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 4
affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.


--- page 3 ---
§4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Classification is made by the Manager, Distribution Protection Engineering, on receipt of Form ER-11.
Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

[P/Heading 2] 4.1 Screen A — aggregate DER on ALN-214
[P/Normal] The 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report (380 applications) contains no ALN-214 row, and neither it nor the On-Hold Queue Report (140 applications) contains a Bramwick Commons row. The On-Hold export has no feeder field, so it cannot independently rule out an on-hold ALN-214 project; no on-hold project is identified as Bramwick or Larkspur. The Existing-DER Register Extract does not carry a feeder field; it contains no Bramwick row. The only Larkspur-named site is Larkspur Warehouse PV, 550 kW, at 950 Larkspur Avenue, Darnwick, with no feeder assignment in the extract. On the identified record, the ALN-214 aggregate is therefore the requested 1,800 kW; any on-hold project later mapped to ALN-214 would be additive. If the 550 kW Larkspur Warehouse PV is later confirmed on ALN-214, the aggregate becomes 2,350 kW, still below the 4,900 kW published available capacity and also below the 2,400 kW daytime minimum.
[P/Normal] DIS-01 Rev 4 does not state a separate numeric percentage for the Screen A penetration threshold; the feeder capacity limit of record is the 4.9 MW published available capacity in HCM-2024-Q2. Applying that limit, Screen A passes. The cross-reference gap between SRP-3 Screen A and DIS-01 is a standards-clarification item for Standards Engineering; it is not a screen failure and does not support a queue hold (ERP-9 Rev 2 §4 and Bulletin EB-2025-03).
[P/Heading 2] 4.2 Screen B — voltage regulation and flicker
[P/Normal] The most recent planning study of record for ALN-214 is dated 12/2023 (HCM-2024-Q2, last study date). At 07/14/2025 that is 19 months old, within the 24-month limit in SRP-3 Screen B. The map carries 4.9 MW of published available capacity for a pure-generation feeder. The 1.8 MW request is 36.7% of that headroom, and no voltage or flicker constraint on ALN-214 is recorded. Screen B passes at the screening level. Final steady-state voltage, regulator/LTC operation under reverse flow, and flicker compliance remain part of the interconnection design and study record; this memo does not substitute for that work.
[P/Heading 2] 4.3 Screen C — short-circuit contribution
[P/Normal] Bramwick is an inverter-based solar facility. Taking the inverter fault contribution at 1.2 × rated output as a screening estimate, 1.8 MW gives 2.16 MVA of fault contribution, or approximately 100 A at 12.47 kV. That is a small increment against distribution feeder fault levels and does not credibly move any feeder protective device from below to above 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor collapse a downstream coordination margin. Screen C passes at screening. The site-specific DPS-07 protection coordination study, POI recloser settings, and any transfer-trip determination remain conditions of interconnection and must be completed before energization. No feeder protective-device ratings or fault study are in the record before 07/14/2025; if the DPS-07 study finds any device above 87.5% of its interrupting rating or a coordination margin below the DPS-07 value, Screen C fails and the application is routed to study.
[P/Heading 2] 4.4 Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load
[P/Normal] Screen D passes: 1,800 kW requested is below the 2,400 kW daytime-window minimum. The full calculation, data-quality review and exclusions are in Section 5.
[P/Heading 2] 4.5 Screen E — reverse power at the substation
[P/Normal] The aggregate DER on ALN-214 (1,800 kW on the record) is below the lowest sustained feeder load in the 12-month AMI record, 1,985 kW at 2025-01-19 07:30, and below the 2,400 kW daytime minimum. The feeder therefore remains load-serving; no reverse power reaches the Larkspur Ridge substation transformer, and no reverse-power setting is required to make this screen pass. If the 550 kW Larkspur Warehouse PV were confirmed on ALN-214, the daytime aggregate of 2,350 kW would still be below the 2,400 kW daytime minimum, and at night that PV unit is not generating, so the aggregate remains 1,800 kW. The 2,350 kW sensitivity has only 50 kW (2.1%) of daytime margin, so any later addition on ALN-214 must be re-screened. Final reverse-power protection remains subject to the DPS-07 site determination. No substation transformer certified reverse-power capability is stated in the records before 07/14/2025; if a capability below 1,800 kW is later found on the transformer record, Screen E must be rerun.
[P/Heading 1] 5. Screen D calculation and data review
[P/Heading 2] 5.1 Method required by SRP-3 Rev 3 §4
[P/Normal] The screen uses the minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent complete twelve calendar months, at 15-minute intervals aligned to the feeder collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within the window. The absolute overnight minimum must not be used. Requested DER capacity must be less than or equal to that daytime minimum. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recompute the Bramwick Screen D / aggregate figures from the source files."""
import json, statistics
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import openpyxl

AMI='/filesystem/Studies/ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx'

def load_ami(path=AMI):
    wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(path,data_only=True,read_only=True)
    ws=wb.active
    rows=[(r[0],r[1]) for r in ws.iter_rows(min_row=5,values_only=True) if r[0] is not None and r[1] is not None]
    return rows

def compute(rows):
    rows=sorted(rows)
    first,last=rows[0][0],rows[-1][0]
    diffs={(rows[i+1][0]-rows[i][0]).total_seconds()/60 for i in range(len(rows)-1)}
    days=len({t.date() for t,_ in rows})
    daytime=[(t,v) for t,v in rows if 10 <= t.hour < 16]
    day_min=min(daytime,key=lambda x:(x[1],x[0]))
    abs_min=min(rows,key=lambda x:(x[1],x[0]))
    # flag single-interval downward excursions > 20% from 5-point local median
    anomalies=[]
    for i in range(2,len(rows)-2):
        neigh=[rows[j][1] for j in range(i-2,i+3) if j!=i]
        med=statistics.median(neigh)
        if rows[i][1] < med*0.8:
            anomalies.append((rows[i][0],rows[i][1],med))
    anom_times={a[0] for a in anomalies}
    day_clean=[(t,v) for t,v in daytime if t not in anom_times]
    abs_clean=[(t,v) for t,v in rows if t not in anom_times]
    day_min_clean=min(day_clean,key=lambda x:(x[1],x[0]))
    abs_min_clean=min(abs_clean,key=lambda x:(x[1],x[0]))
    return dict(first=first.isoformat(),last=last.isoformat(),records=len(rows),days=days,
                cadence_minutes=sorted(diffs),daytime_records=len(daytime),
                day_min_kw=day_min[1],day_min_time=day_min[0].isoformat(),
                day_min_clean_kw=day_min_clean[1],day_min_clean_time=day_min_clean[0].isoformat(),
                abs_min_kw=abs_min[1],abs_min_time=abs_min[0].isoformat(),
                abs_min_clean_kw=abs_min_clean[1],abs_min_clean_time=abs_min_clean[0].isoformat(),
                anomalies=[(t.isoformat(),v,med) for t,v,med in anomalies])

if __name__=='__main__':
    print(json.dumps(compute(load_ami()),indent=2))

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW SCREEN DETERMINATION
To:      Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
From:   Priya Ranganathan, Interconnection Studies
Date:   06/25/2025
Subject: Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW, Feeder ALN-214) — Supplemental Review Screen Determination
1. Project
The application was routed to supplemental review following failure of an initial fast-track screen. This memo records the disposition of the 100%-of-minimum-load screen applied under SRP-3 Rev 3.
2. Screen applied
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar, per §4 of SRP-3 (Rev 3, effective 02/10/2025). Under this screen, the requested DER capacity is compared against the minimum load observed on the subject feeder from AMI interval data.
3. Analysis
Reviewed AMI interval load data for Feeder ALN-214 from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse and identified a minimum feeder load of 1.1 MW. The value was drawn from the feeder AMI record available on file for ALN-214. No intervals were excluded for known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching during the period reviewed.
4. Comparison
1.8 MW requested exceeds 1.1 MW minimum feeder load — screen FAILED.
5. Recommendation
Study Agreement required prior to advancement. The application should not proceed on the supplemental-review track. A Study Agreement should be offered to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC, with the scope covering the technical conditions that gave rise to the failed screen on Feeder ALN-214.
6. Disposition
Return supplemental review file to Interconnection Studies queue with a failed-screen flag on Feeder ALN-214.
Notify the applicant of the screen result and forward the Study Agreement package.
Hold advancement of PXA record for Bramwick Commons Solar until Study Agreement is executed.

# Asks in the instruction and where each is answered

1. **Review `Bramwick_Commons_Screening_Memo_v1.docx` against `ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx` and the DER Program records as of 07/14/2025.**
   - Answered in memo §6 (reconciliation table), §2 (records reviewed), §5 (AMI recalculation).
   - Finding: v1's 1.1 MW is the single 2025-03-23 03:45 absolute-overnight excursion, not the SRP-3 §4 daytime minimum; v1's stated 06/24/2024–06/24/2025 window and 60-minute cadence do not match the 15-minute 07/01/2024–06/30/2025 AMI file.

2. **Issue the memo the procedure calls for (SRP-3 Rev 3 §6).**
   - Memo is `Bramwick_Commons_Screen_Memo.docx`; it contains §6(a) application/applicant/feeder/capacity, §6(b) Screens A–E with pass/fail, §6(c) Screen D minimum/data window/interval count/exclusions, §6(d) disposition, §6(e) signatures/date, §6(f) superseded memo identifier.

3. **State the disposition the procedure produces.**

---
name: der-interconnection-screening
description: Utility DER interconnection screens and reports - fast-track and supplemental review screens (15 % of peak, minimum load from AMI interval data), pre-application capacity reports from queue data, certified equipment lists and witness tests. Use for DER/solar/storage interconnection review tasks.
---

# DER interconnection screening, pre-application reports and certified equipment
Frameworks: FERC SGIP (Order 2006, revised by Order 792) and state rules modelled on it (CA Rule 21, NY SIR, others).
The utility's own tariff/procedure in the record governs: cite its sections and use its thresholds where they differ.

## Fast track / initial review screens (SGIP 2.2.1; Rule 21 Initial Review has equivalents)
Eligibility: size by line voltage and distance from substation, certified equipment (Order 792 table). Screens:
radial circuit; aggregate generation on the line section (existing + queued ahead + proposed) <= 15 % of line-section
annual peak load (section bounded by automatic sectionalizing devices or end of line); spot network limits;
fault contribution <= 10 % of circuit maximum at the primary nearest the POI; protective devices <= 87.5 % of
interrupting rating; transformer/grounding configuration (effectively grounded on 4-wire primary); shared
single-phase secondary <= 20 kW, service imbalance <= 20 % of transformer rating; transient-stability areas (10 MW);
no utility upgrades required. A failure is not a rejection: offer an options meeting / supplemental review.

## Supplemental review (SGIP 2.4.4; Rule 21 Screens N, O, P)
1. Minimum load (penetration) screen: aggregate generation on the line section < 100 % of minimum load, for every
   line section bounded by automatic sectionalizing devices upstream of the POI, using 12 months of data.
   - Solar PV without storage: daytime minimum, 10:00-16:00 for fixed-tilt (08:00-18:00 for trackers, SGIP);
     all other generation (incl. PV + storage that can discharge at night): absolute minimum over all hours.
   - Aggregate = existing interconnected + queued ahead of this request + proposed, nameplate AC (or certified
     export limit / net injection if station load is served on site). Do not count generation already reflected
     in the load data (net AMI reads at PV customers); exclude later-queued and withdrawn projects. If minimum load
     cannot be determined, the results must state why.
2. Voltage and power quality: steady-state voltage held in ANSI C84.1 Range A under all conditions incl. reverse
   flow through regulators/LTCs (bidirectional/cogeneration mode), voltage fluctuation/flicker (IEEE 1453 or
   utility practice), harmonics (IEEE 519 / IEEE 1547 limits).
3. Safety and reliability: protection coordination and fuse saving, reclosing vs inverter cease-to-energize time,
   islanding risk when generation approaches load, ground-fault overvoltage, need for transfer trip, load dominated
   by few customers or concentrated near the end of line, distance from substation.
Outcome: pass all -> interconnection agreement (possibly with minor modifications). Fail any -> name the screen and
margin, and the options: modify (reduce size, certified export limit/power control), study process (system impact /
facilities study at customer cost), or withdraw. Never "pass" a failing screen by judgement; keep judgement separate.

## Minimum load from AMI / interval data (script it, show the steps)
- Units: energy per interval (kWh) -> kW = kWh x 60 / interval minutes (x4 for 15-min); MW vs kW; delivered vs
  received channels (net load = delivered - received).
- Sum meters per timestamp, then take the minimum (never sum each meter's own minimum). Window: local time,
  interval-beginning vs -ending stamps, DST duplicates/gaps, only intervals inside the window, 12 months to as-of.
- Scope: line section(s) upstream of the POI, not feeder/substation unless only that exists (say so); check meter-
  to-section mapping and abnormal configurations (load transfers).
- Data quality: zeros, blanks, flagged/estimated reads, outages, spikes are not minimum load; state how many were
  excluded and why, and give the result both ways if exclusion changes it.
- Report: minimum, its timestamp, source, interval count, generation itemised by project, ratio, margin, pass/fail.

## Supplemental review memo of record
Contents: application/queue ID, size (AC, DC, storage, export limit), feeder/line section, procedure and edition,
data used and as-of date, each screen with basis, numbers and result, disposition and applicant's next step,
assumptions, preparer and reviewer/countersignature blocks.
To correct an issued document, issue a new revision that says what changed and why; it needs its own review and
approval.

## Pre-application report / capacity request (SGIP 1.2)
- The utility supplies existing data only (no study): total capacity of the substation/bank and circuit likely to
  serve the site, existing aggregate generation, aggregate queued generation, available capacity, single vs three
  phase and distance, peak and minimum load (daytime and absolute) when available, regulators/protective devices
  between site and substation, network service, known constraints.
- Pre-application data are informational, as of a stated date, non-binding and confer no queue position (SGIP 1.2);
  say so. The request is not an interconnection application; capacity is allocated by queue order when a complete
  application is filed and studied.
- Available capacity = applicable limit (hosting capacity, thermal rating or screen limit stated in the record) -
  in-service generation - active queue on the same feeder/section. Count active statuses (application complete,
  in study, ISA signed, under construction, awaiting PTO) and in-service; exclude withdrawn, rejected, expired,
  cancelled, duplicates, other feeders and pre-app requests. Use AC nameplate or certified export limit (not DC);
  storage counts at its export capability. Check MW/kW columns.
- Compare the requested size with the result (exceeds -> likely study/upgrades). Check any figure the requester
  quotes against the record.

## Certified equipment and witness tests
- Certification: NRTL listing to UL 1741; SB = IEEE 1547.1-2020 tests for IEEE 1547-2018 (SA: older Rule 21);
  state lists (e.g. CEC grid-support inverters) and the utility's Certified Equipment List.
- Carriage check per site: check the as-built record of installed equipment (manufacturer, full model number incl.
  suffix/rating variant, firmware or software version, certification standard) against the list revision in force on
  the as-of date (delisted, superseded, expired entries do not count).
- Not carried -> type test / certification, or field verification witnessed by the utility (IEEE 1547-2018 clause 11
  test & verification, IEEE 1547.1-2020 procedures): unintentional islanding (cease to energize within 2 s),
  voltage/frequency trip and clearing times, ride-through category settings, enter-service / reconnect delay and
  ramp, open-phase response, voltage/reactive and frequency-watt functions, export/power-control limit, disconnect
  and interlock operation, protective relay functional tests if relay-based, applied settings vs utility profile.
- Customer/installer (often with manufacturer or commissioning agent) performs; utility witnesses. On file first:
  approved application/agreement,
  AHJ final, as-built single-line, site plan, settings file and firmware evidence, test procedure accepted in
  advance, data sheets and certificates, relay settings, test equipment calibration, switching order.

name: engineering-deliverables
description: Method for engineering design and calculation packages graded against requirements - document precedence, superseded documents, requirement/constraint registers, hard-constraint checks, unit discipline, optimisation within constraints, and schema-exact deliverable files (CSV, JSON, XLSX, ZIP, IFC). Use for any task that asks for calculations, a design, a plan, a schedule, a register or a structured submission.
---

# Engineering deliverables

## 1. Know exactly what is graded
- Copy every deliverable requirement from the instruction into `/tmp/ahpele/checklist.md`: path, file name, format,
  required columns/keys/tokens (exact spelling), units, row granularity ("one row per X and Y"), and any scoring rule.
- The instruction is a data contract. Use its column names, token vocabularies and IDs verbatim. Extra columns are
  usually harmless; missing or renamed ones are not.
- If the instruction states how the work is scored (e.g. hard constraints gate the score, cost objective, recall of a
  register), let that decide where effort goes: never trade a hard constraint for objective value.

## 2. Document precedence and status
- Read the governing specification first: it usually lists which standards, revisions and documents apply.
- Typical precedence (unless the project documents say otherwise): addenda / RFI responses / site instructions issued
  later > specification > drawings > schedules > vendor data > reference standards. Later dated responses override
  earlier ones on the same point.
- A document marked superseded, cancelled, withdrawn, void or draft, or an older revision of a document that exists in
  a newer revision, is not an authority. Do not cite it, do not take values from it. Record in your narrative that you
  saw it and why you set it aside.
- Words like "cancelled" inside a document's text often describe another document. Check before discarding.

## 3. Requirements table and register
- Before designing, list every hard requirement with: id, document, clause/table, requirement, limit value, unit, what
  it binds (which items). Save as `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv`.
- Hard requirements include: safety and code limits, permit/authorisation limits (discharge, noise, setbacks),
  capacities (power, flow, head, load), resource caps (equipment, crews, water, budget), milestones and deadlines.
- If a register is a deliverable, build it from this table. Cite real project documents and clauses, not the brief.
  Cite only documents that are in force.

## 4. Calculations
- Work in one unit system internally; convert at the boundary. Keep inputs, intermediate results and units in a script
  (`/tmp/ahpele/calc.py`) so numbers can be recomputed after every change.
- Take every input from a document you can cite; write assumptions down where the documents leave a choice.
- Cross-check: totals equal sums of parts, the same quantity has the same value in every file, schedules respect
  durations and predecessors, quantities respect the caps.

## 5. Build early, then improve
- Produce a complete first version of every deliverable early with conservative choices that satisfy all hard
  requirements, even if it is not optimal. An incomplete or missing file scores nothing.
- Never write placeholders (TBD, NaN, "to be determined") in a numeric field. If a value is genuinely not applicable,
  use the not-applicable convention the instruction allows (often blank, N/A or NONE).

## 6. Verify with code
- Write `/tmp/ahpele/check.py` that loads your deliverable files exactly as written and tests every requirement row and
  every checklist item (columns, tokens, units, ranges, cross-file consistency). Run it after every change.
- Run the format checker: `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <deliverable paths>`.
- For CAD/BIM outputs, re-open the file with the standard library you wrote it with and check the entities, property
  sets and attributes the instruction names.
- IFC written by hand (no BIM library): generate it with a small script, not by typing STEP lines. Copy each entity
  pattern from the example file the task provides (or from the schema), keep every attribute in order (use `$` for an
  unset one; an IfcBuildingStorey has 10 attributes, an IfcPropertySet 5, an IfcRelDefinesByProperties 6), write every REAL
  with a decimal point (`20.` or `20.0`, never `20` and never `4.5.`; coordinates, directions, depths, elevations), and double apostrophes inside strings. Run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_ifc.py <file>` until it reports 0 errors, and compare its structure printout
  (storeys and elevations, property sets, footprints, heights) with what the contract requires. One unreadable
  entity can make the whole file unreadable.
- Placed or routed 3D models (coordination models, MEP routing, layouts): verify the FILE, not your script's variables.
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_clash.py <file.ifc> --point <entry x,y,z>` re-reads it with ifcopenshell's geometry
  engine in world coordinates and lists clashing pairs, element classes stacked at one spot, broken runs and the
  distance from each run to the entry point. Coordinates in `IfcCartesianPoint` are in the project length unit (a
  millimetre project takes millimetres); library helpers such as `ifcopenshell.api` placement calls take SI metres and
  convert for you, so do not divide by 1000 by hand as well. Iterate until 0 clashes and one network per service.

## 7. Optimise last
- Only after all hard checks pass: improve the objective (cost, performance) with a systematic search (enumerate
  options, or scipy.optimize when available), re-running the checks for every candidate. Keep the best feasible plan
  on disk at all times.

§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common

§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.

Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.

§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and

# Independent review — `Bramwick_Commons_Screen_Memo.docx`

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Scope: the single Word deliverable at `/filesystem/Bramwick_Commons_Screen_Memo.docx`, the countersigned v1 memo, the ALN-214 AMI workbook, and the DER Program records as of 07/14/2025. I reopened the DOCX, parsed every paragraph and table, re-read the governing procedures and the queue/register/HCM/SIS records, and recomputed the Screen D values from the AMI workbook with my own script. I did not modify any deliverable.

The memo is well presented and its core Screen D arithmetic is correct (see "Verified correct" at the end). The findings below are about the **determinations that the record does not support**, the **disposition**, and the **missing application record**.

## Findings, most serious first

### 1. BLOCKING — The overall disposition is wrong: the procedure requires a study agreement where a screen is inconclusive, and the memo passes screens it admits are not supported by the record.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 Rev 3 §2 (p.1): "Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application **shall be advanced to a study agreement** rather than passed or failed under this procedure." SRP-3 §6(b) requires "the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each"; §6(d) requires the recommended disposition. The RA tasking memo of 07/01/2025 §5 (R0089) reinforces this: "Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported."
- **What the deliverable has.** §1, §4.1, §4.3, §4.5 and §7 state: "All SRP-3 Screens A–E pass on the record" and "advance without study agreement." At the same time:
  - §4.1: "The On-Hold export has no feeder field, so it cannot independently rule out an on-hold ALN-214 project"; the Existing-DER Register "does not carry a feeder field."
  - §4.3: "No feeder protective-device ratings or fault study are in the record before 07/14/2025"; "if the DPS-07 study finds any device above 87.5% of its interrupting rating ... Screen C fails."
  - §4.5: "No substation transformer certified reverse-power capability is stated in the records before 07/14/2025"; "if a capability below 1,800 kW is later found ... Screen E must be rerun."
  - §4.2: "final steady-state voltage, regulator/LTC operation under reverse flow, and flicker compliance remain part of the interconnection design and study record."
- **What it should be.** Screen D passes (1,800 kW ≤ 2,400 kW). Screens A, C and E are **inconclusive on the record**, and Screen B is at best a conditional/deferred pass. Under SRP-3 §2 the application must be **advanced to a study agreement**, with the study scoped to the unresolved screens (feeder aggregate/queue mapping, voltage/flicker, protective-device fault duty/coordination, transformer reverse-power capability and settings). A "PASS at screening" with the actual test deferred is not a pass/fail determination under §6(b), and a pass by engineering judgment is expressly not permitted by the procedure's inconclusive-result rule.
- **Evidence.** SRP-3 Rev 3 pp.1–3, §§2, 3, 6; memo §§4.1–4.5, 7, 8; RA-2025-07-01 §5. The memo's own admissions are the evidence; no external assumption is needed.

### 2. BLOCKING — There is no application identifier, PXA/queue number or queue position, so SRP-3 §6(a) is not met and the "advance" disposition cannot be implemented in queue order.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §6(a): the memo "shall contain ... application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity." Tariff §12.3: "A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be returned with a written deficiency notice..." Tariff §12.7 requires processing in queue order. RA tasking memo §1 (R0079): "Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture and next required action."
- **What the deliverable has.** Table 3, "Application identifier / file": "IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 (v1 memo file; this memo is IS-BRAM-2025-07-14 v2). No PXA/queue number is stated in the 06/25/2025 memo; the 07/14/2025 active queue contains no ALN-214 row, and neither queue export contains a Bramwick Commons row. The Program is to insert the PXA number when the queue record is corrected." §8 calls this "an administrative record gap, not a technical screen failure." The action table schedules insertion of the PXA number for 07/18/2025 — after the determination is issued.
- **What it should be.** A verified PXA application number and queue date/position from the application record, or a return-to-applicant deficiency notice under Tariff §12.3. The memo cannot be the "memo of record for the Bramwick Commons Solar application" while the application identifier is the v1 memo's document number. The requested capacity (1.8 MW) is likewise sourced to the v1 memo, not to the applicant's filed application (SRP-3 §5(e) makes the application record authoritative for the filed capacity, single-line, inverter specifications and control narrative).
- **Evidence.** Memo Table 3 and §8; 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report (380 data rows, no ALN-214/Bramwick row); On-Hold Queue Report (140 rows, no Bramwick row; no feeder field); SIS Backlog (no Bramwick/ALN-214 row); Nextcloud `/DER_Program/Applications` (7 files, none Bramwick); Tariff §12.3 and §12.7. The v1 memo itself has no PXA number.

### 3. BLOCKING — Screen A is not a pass: DIS-01 contains no numeric penetration threshold, the 4.9 MW HCM figure is not a threshold, and the aggregate is incomplete.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §3 Screen A: "Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01." SRP-3 §5(c): the active-queue and on-hold registers are authoritative; "Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen A." SRP-3 §5: substitution of a source not listed "shall be documented in the memo, together with the reason for the substitution."
- **What the deliverable has.** §4.1/Table 4-1: "Requested 1,800 kW + identified existing 0 kW + identified active-queue 0 kW = 1,800 kW. ALN-214 published available capacity is 4,900 kW (HCM-2024-Q2)." It then says: "DIS-01 Rev 4 does not state a separate numeric percentage for the Screen A penetration threshold; the feeder capacity limit of record is the 4.9 MW published available capacity in HCM-2024-Q2. Applying that limit, Screen A passes." It admits the on-hold export has no feeder field and the existing-DER register has no feeder field.
- **What it should be.** Screen A is **inconclusive**, not a pass. (i) DIS-01 Rev 4 contains no numeric penetration threshold at all (the word "penetration" appears only in SRP-3 Screen A; DIS-01's Table 3-1 gives class ranges and review paths, not a threshold). The 4.9 MW HCM value is a published *available capacity*, not a DIS-01 threshold. (ii) HCM-2024-Q2 Title Block A16 says the published values "do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date" and applicants "should consult Distribution Planning for confirmation before finalizing project sizing decisions"; the map's refresh commitment is quarterly, and this value is from a 12/2023 study published 05/15/2024. (iii) The aggregate cannot be built because the on-hold and existing-DER registers carry no feeder field; the memo's own §4.1 says it cannot rule out an on-hold ALN-214 project. Under SRP-3 §2 the application must go to a study agreement (or the missing feeder mappings and a Distribution Planning confirmation must be obtained and the screen re-run). The memo's referral of the cross-reference gap to Standards Engineering for 07/28/2025 does not cure an inconclusive screen result and does not make "advance without study agreement" valid.
- **Evidence.** SRP-3 §3 Screen A and §5(c); DIS-01 Rev 4 full text (no numeric penetration threshold); HCM-2024-Q2 `Feeder Capacity` row ALN-214 (4.9 MW, last study 12/2023) and Title Block A16; memo §4.1.

### 4. MAJOR — Screen C is not a pass: no feeder protective-device ratings or fault study are in the record, so the 87.5%/DPS-07 test was not performed.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §3 Screen C: "DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to fall below the values specified in DPS-07." DPS-07 §5.1(c) requires coordination time-current characteristics documented in the site protection coordination study before energization.
- **What the deliverable has.** §4.3: a 1.2 × 1.8 MW = 2.16 MVA estimate, "approximately 100 A at 12.47 kV"; "No feeder device is identified as approaching 87.5% of its interrupting rating"; "No feeder protective-device ratings or fault study are in the record before 07/14/2025; if the DPS-07 study finds any device above 87.5% ... Screen C fails." The 1.2× factor is not taken from Bramwick's application or inverter data (there is no Bramwick application in the record).
- **What it should be.** The screen requires comparing the incremental DER fault contribution against each feeder protective device's interrupting rating and the DPS-07 coordination margins. Without the device ratings, existing fault currents and coordination settings, the 100 A estimate cannot establish that no device crosses 87.5% or that coordination margins hold. This is an inconclusive screen and, under SRP-3 §2, a study-agreement item. "Does not credibly move" is judgment, not a hard-limit check.
- **Evidence.** SRP-3 Screen C; DPS-07 Rev 2 §5.1(c); memo §4.3. The memo itself states the necessary data are absent.

### 5. MAJOR — Screen E is not a pass: the transformer's certified reverse-power capability and settings are not in the record, and the substation aggregate is incomplete.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §3 Screen E: "Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in place, the application shall be routed to study." DPS-07 §4.2 item 3 requires the ANSI 32 directional-power element; DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 3 requires it on the POI recloser for a pure-generation site.
- **What the deliverable has.** §4.5: aggregate 1,800 kW is below the 1,985 kW "night minimum" and 2,400 kW daytime minimum; "no reverse power reaches the Larkspur Ridge substation transformer, and no reverse-power setting is required to make this screen pass"; "No substation transformer certified reverse-power capability is stated in the records before 07/14/2025; if a capability below 1,800 kW is later found ... Screen E must be rerun." It also says the 2,350 kW sensitivity has only 50 kW (2.1%) of daytime margin.
- **What it should be.** The screen has two independent triggers: (a) aggregate DER > transformer certified reverse-power capability; (b) reverse-power protective settings not in place. The memo tests neither. A load-versus-generation comparison is not the screen's capability test. The memo must obtain the Larkspur Ridge transformer's certified reverse-power capability and the reverse-power settings, and aggregate all DER on that transformer. HCM-2024-Q2 shows **ALN-205 and ALN-214 both at Larkspur Ridge**; the 07/14/2025 Active Queue contains **PXA-2024-0077 Brackenhaven Community Solar, 1.8 MW, ALN-205** (system impact study; SIS-2025-023). A transformer serving both feeders could see 1,800 + 1,800 kW plus any existing DER. The memo's ALN-214-only 1,800 kW comparison does not establish the transformer capability or the settings. Screen E is inconclusive → study agreement. The 50 kW (2.1%) sensitivity also means the pass should not be issued until the 550 kW Larkspur Warehouse feeder assignment is confirmed.
- **Evidence.** SRP-3 Screen E; DPS-07 §4.2; DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 3; HCM-2024-Q2 rows ALN-205/ALN-214 (both Larkspur Ridge); Active Queue PXA-2024-0077 (1.8 MW, ALN-205, system impact study); SIS Backlog SIS-2025-023; memo §4.5.

### 6. MAJOR — Screen B is not a pass: the planning study was not reviewed and flicker was not addressed.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §3 Screen B: "Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record." The screen covers "Voltage regulation and flicker."
- **What the deliverable has.** §4.2: "The most recent planning study of record for ALN-214 is dated 12/2023 (HCM-2024-Q2, last study date), 19 months before 07/14/2025, so within the 24-month limit. Published available capacity 4,900 kW; no voltage or flicker constraint is recorded. ... Screen B passes at the screening level. Final steady-state voltage, regulator/LTC operation under reverse flow, and flicker compliance remain part of the interconnection design and study record."
- **What it should be.** The HCM's "Last Study Date" is a metadata field, not the planning study, and the HCM's stated basis (Title Block A12: recorded peak/minimum load, existing DER, "standard thermal / voltage / protection screens") does not include flicker. The memo did not review the 12/2023 ALN-214 planning study (none is in the record) and did not perform a screening voltage-rise calculation. "No constraint is recorded" is absence of evidence, not a pass. Voltage regulation under reverse flow and flicker are part of Screen B, not deferred design checks. Screen B is inconclusive → study agreement.
- **Evidence.** SRP-3 Screen B; HCM-2024-Q2 Title Block A12/A16 (basis and caveats); memo §4.2.

### 7. MAJOR — DIS-01 Table 3-1's medium-scale review path is a system impact study; the memo classifies Bramwick as medium-scale but says "advance without study agreement" without resolving the conflict.

- **Requirement.** DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 3-1: "Medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW | In DER Program scope | Initial screening + system impact study | Table 5-1, Category 3." DIS-01 §8 and ERP-9 §3 require standards conflicts to be routed via Form ER-11 for a per-site determination.
- **What the deliverable has.** Table 3: "Facility class | Medium-scale DER, 1 MW–5 MW (DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Table 3-1)." §1/§7: "advance without study agreement." §8: "DIS-01 §4 allows a facility that does not pass an initial screen to be evaluated under SRP-3 or to advance to a system impact study; the 'advance without a study agreement' call is the SRP-3 disposition and does not waive any study ... separately imposed by DIS-01."
- **What it should be.** The memo cannot both cite Table 3-1's medium-scale review path and issue a no-study disposition without a per-site determination of the conflict between Table 3-1 and SRP-3 §2(b) (which lists medium-scale in supplemental review). If Table 3-1 governs, the disposition is a system impact study/study agreement; if SRP-3 governs, the memo must say why and route the conflict under ERP-9. The memo's §8 wording ("does not waive any study") is inconsistent with the §1/§7 call and does not tell the reader which path applies.
- **Evidence.** DIS-01 Table 3-1 and §8; SRP-3 §2(b); ERP-9 §3; memo Table 3, §7, §8.

### 8. MINOR — Screen E's night statement is physically wrong.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 Screen E; basic operating-state check.
- **What the deliverable has.** §4.5: "If the 550 kW Larkspur Warehouse PV were confirmed on ALN-214, the daytime aggregate of 2,350 kW would still be below the 2,400 kW daytime minimum, and at night that PV unit is not generating, so the aggregate remains 1,800 kW."
- **What it should be.** At night the Bramwick solar facility is also not generating, so the aggregate is 0 kW, not 1,800 kW. The 1,800 kW figure is nameplate/requested capacity, not night output. The error does not change the Screen E conclusion, but it misstates the operating state and could confuse the reverse-flow analysis.
- **Evidence.** Memo §4.5; Bramwick is solar PV (memo Table 3); the 2,400 kW minimum is a daytime load, the 1,985 kW minimum is at 07:30 (before solar output).

### 9. MINOR — The memo uses feeder-aggregate AMI data without stating whether the POI line section is the whole feeder.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §4 requires feeder AMI interval data; the DER screening skill's minimum-load method scopes the check to the line section(s) upstream of the POI unless only feeder-level data exist, and requires that limitation to be stated.
- **What the deliverable has.** §5.2 uses "Feeder Load (kW)" from the ALN-214 export and calls it the feeder minimum. It does not state whether the POI is at the feeder head or whether there are line sections/reclosers downstream of the POI.
- **What it should be.** State that feeder-level AMI is the only published data for ALN-214 (if so), or obtain the line-section data upstream of the POI. If the POI is not at the feeder head, the relevant minimum load could be lower than 2,400 kW, and the 1,800 kW pass could change. This is a scope limitation that should be recorded in §8.
- **Evidence.** AMI header "Feeder: ALN-214 ... Feeder Load (kW)"; memo §5.2/§8; no line-section or POI-location record in the file.

### 10. MINOR — The v1 memo is not actually flagged superseded in the file, and the stale ALN-214 wiki page is not corrected, contrary to SRP-3 §6 and the author's summary.

- **Requirement.** SRP-3 §6: "Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover."

SRP-3 §6(b) requires "the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each"; §6(d) requires the recommended disposition. The RA tasking memo of 07/01/2025 §5 (R0089) reinforces this: "Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported."
- **What the deliverable has.** §1, §4.1, §4.3, §4.5 and §7 state: "All SRP-3 Screens A–E pass on the record" and "advance without study agreement." At the same time:
