exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "

def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return {x}
    out = {x, f"{v:g}"}

        out.add(str(int(v)))

def read_register(path):
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xlsm")):

        except ImportError:
            sys.exit("--register on .xlsx needs openpyxl; export the sheet to CSV")
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)
        rows = []
        for ws in wb.worksheets:
            rows += [["" if c is None else str(c) for c in r] for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]

1. Project
The application was routed to supplemental review following failure of an initial fast-track screen. This memo records the disposition of the 100%-of-minimum-load screen applied under SRP-3 Rev 3.
2. Screen applied
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar, per §4 of SRP-3 (Rev 3, effective 02/10/2025). Under this screen, the requested DER capacity is compared against the minimum load observed on the subject feeder from AMI interval data.
3. Analysis
Reviewed AMI interval load data for Feeder ALN-214 from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse and identified a minimum feeder load of 1.1 MW. The value was drawn from the feeder AMI record available on file for ALN-214. No intervals were excluded for known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching during the period reviewed.
4. Comparison
1.8 MW requested exceeds 1.1 MW minimum feeder load — screen FAILED.
5. Recommendation
Study Agreement required prior to advancement. The application should not proceed on the supplemental-review track. A Study Agreement should be offered to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC, with the scope covering the technical conditions that gave rise to the failed screen on Feeder ALN-214.
6. Disposition
Return supplemental review file to Interconnection Studies queue with a failed-screen flag on Feeder ALN-214.
Notify the applicant of the screen result and forward the Study Agreement package.
Hold advancement of PXA record for Bramwick Commons Solar until Study Agreement is executed.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE

4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com

SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW DETERMINATION

Bramwick Commons Solar — Feeder ALN-214

Revision 2  ·  Supersedes IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 v1 dated 06/25/2025

To:  Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies

From:  Priya Ranganathan, Staff Analyst, Interconnection Studies

Date:  07/14/2025

Subject:  Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW, Feeder ALN-214) — Supplemental Review Determination, Revision 2

cc:  Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs; Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group



1. Determination

Answer first. The 06/25/2025 v1 Screen D failure does not stand. On the ALN-214 15-minute AMI record, the 10:00–16:00 daytime minimum is 2,400 kW at 2025-02-12 11:30. The 1,800 kW request is below that minimum by 600 kW (25.0%), so Screen D PASSES. The v1 memo IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 is superseded in full.

The record does not, however, support a “pass all screens / advance without study” disposition. Screen A is INCONCLUSIVE because DIS-01 Rev 4 contains no numeric penetration threshold and the feeder aggregate cannot be completed from the available registers. Screen B is INCONCLUSIVE because no ALN-214 planning study is on file and the hosting-capacity map does not address flicker. Screen C is INCONCLUSIVE because no feeder protective-device ratings, fault study or coordination settings are in the record. Screen E is INCONCLUSIVE because no transformer certified reverse-power capability or reverse-power settings are in the record and the Larkspur Ridge transformer aggregate is incomplete. Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §2, an inconclusive screen result requires the application to be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed.

Disposition: ADVANCE TO STUDY AGREEMENT. The study agreement is the SRP-3 §2 outcome for the four inconclusive screens and is also the review path stated for a medium-scale facility in DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 3-1. Because the file also lacks a complete application and a PXA/queue number, the file is returned to the applicant with a Tariff §12.3 deficiency notice; the study agreement is to be executed only after the complete application, PXA and queue position are on record. The v1 memo is not the determination of record.


2. Application and records reviewed

The following records as they stood at 07/14/2025 were reviewed. No document dated after 07/14/2025 is used. The application record itself is incomplete; that deficiency is recorded in Table 2-1 and is part of the disposition.

Table 2-1 — Application record


Table 2-2 — Records reviewed


Records note. The ALN-214 wiki summary page (page 51) describes the export as hourly with 8,760 records. That page is not the AMI file and was not used. The §5(a) authoritative source is the 15-minute workbook with 35,040 records; the wiki page is to be corrected so the record does not repeat the v1 cadence error.

3. Governing documents and precedence

The APUC-filed tariff controls where it and DIS-01 address the same topic (DIS-01 §1 and §2; Tariff §12.1). SRP-3 Rev 3 governs supplemental review and Screen D. The following documents are in force and were applied.

Table 3-1 — Governing documents


Documents set aside, and why:


Precedence and conflicts. DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 3-1 states the medium-scale (1 MW–5 MW) review path as “Initial screening + system impact study.” SRP-3 Rev 3 §2(b) includes medium-scale facilities within supplemental review. The two documents therefore point to different review paths on their face. DIS-01 §8 and ERP-9 §3 require a standards conflict encountered in screening or study to be routed via Form ER-11 for a per-site determination; no “winning” document is selected across the program. Pending that determination, this memo applies the stricter path — a study agreement — which is also the result of SRP-3 §2 on the four inconclusive screens. The ER-11 referral is an action in §7; it is not a queue hold (ERP-9 §4; Bulletin EB-2025-03).

Screen A cross-reference. SRP-3 Screen A requires the applicable penetration threshold “set in DIS-01.” DIS-01 Rev 4 contains no numeric penetration threshold: its only threshold is the 500 kW program-scope threshold, and Table 3-1 gives class ranges and review paths. That is a standards silence within ERP-9 §2(2), not a licence to substitute the 4.9 MW hosting-capacity figure. The silence is referred under ERP-9 §3 and is one reason Screen A is inconclusive, not a pass.

4. Screen-by-screen determinations

SRP-3 §3 requires Screens A through E in the order given. SRP-3 §2 recognises a third outcome where the record is insufficient: the result is inconclusive, is neither a pass nor a fail, and requires a study agreement. Table 4-1 records the call for each screen; §§4.1–4.5 give the basis.

Table 4-1 — Screen determinations


4.1 Screen A — aggregate DER on ALN-214

SRP-3 Screen A requires the total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus requested) on the subject feeder not to exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Two independent problems prevent a pass.

(i) There is no numeric threshold in DIS-01. DIS-01 Rev 4 contains no numeric penetration threshold. The word “penetration” does not appear in DIS-01; its only threshold is the 500 kW program-scope threshold, and Table 3-1 gives class ranges and review paths. The 4.9 MW (4,900 kW) ALN-214 figure in HCM-2024-Q2 is expressly “Published Available Capacity” — headroom, not a cap on total nameplate DER. HCM Title Block A16 states that published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date, that the active-queue register is the record of that activity, and that applicants should consult Distribution Planning before finalizing sizing. The 4.9 MW figure is therefore not the Screen A threshold and cannot be used to pass the screen.

(ii) The aggregate cannot be completed. The 07/14/2025 active queue has 380 rows and no ALN-214 row. The on-hold queue has 140 rows and no Bramwick row, but the export carries no feeder field, so an on-hold ALN-214 project cannot be ruled out. The Existing-DER Register has 21 rows and no feeder field; the only Larkspur-named site is Larkspur Warehouse PV, 550 kW, with no feeder assignment. The requested 1.8 MW is itself sourced only to the v1 memo. On the identified record the only ALN-214 DER is the request; the total cannot be stated as a number that would support a pass.

Result: INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass. The cross-reference gap between SRP-3 Screen A and DIS-01 is a standards silence to be resolved under ERP-9 §3 (Form ER-11), not a queue hold. The study agreement scope must include the threshold determination and a complete feeder/queue mapping.

Sensitivity — the 15%-of-peak fast-track screen. SRP-3 §1 refers to the fast-track technical screens “set out in DIS-01 Rev 4,” but DIS-01 does not set them out. The v1 memo says an initial fast-track screen failed but does not identify it. To test whether the omission could mask a failure, the memo also ran the commonly used 15%-of-line-section annual-peak screen as a sensitivity. The ALN-214 annual peak is 8,526 kW at 2024-08-01 13:30; the feeder peak is an upper bound on any line-section peak, so 15% is 1,279 kW. The 1,800 kW request is 21.1% of peak — 521 kW above that sensitivity. This is not used as the formal Screen A determination because no 15% threshold is stated in DIS-01 Rev 4 or in any project document in the record. It reinforces that Screen A cannot be passed on this record: either the threshold is unresolved (inconclusive) or, on the common 15% screen, the request fails. Both outcomes lead to study.

4.2 Screen B — voltage regulation and flicker

SRP-3 Screen B requires review against the feeder’s most recent planning study or, where none is on file for the subject feeder within 24 months, a screening voltage-rise calculation using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record. The screen covers both voltage regulation and flicker.

What the record shows. HCM-2024-Q2 gives the ALN-214 “Last Study Date” as 12/2023, 19 months before 07/14/2025 and within the 24-month limit. But HCM-2024-Q2 is a published hosting-capacity map export, not the planning study. No ALN-214 planning study is in the record. The map’s stated basis is a feeder-level planning study using recorded peak and minimum load, existing DER of record and “standard thermal / voltage / protection screens”; it does not include flicker, and it does not contain the conductor and transformer impedance data needed for a screening voltage-rise calculation. The statement that no voltage or flicker constraint is recorded is an absence of evidence, not a review.

Result: INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass. The study agreement scope must obtain and review the 12/2023 planning study (or perform a screening voltage-rise calculation if the study is not available) and must address steady-state voltage, regulator/LTC operation under reverse flow, and flicker. The final design checks do not substitute for the screen.

4.3 Screen C — short-circuit contribution

SRP-3 Screen C requires that DER short-circuit contribution not cause any feeder protective device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating and not cause any downstream protection coordination margin to fall below the values specified in DPS-07.

What the record shows. No feeder protective-device ratings, existing fault currents or coordination settings are in the record before 07/14/2025. The memo can estimate an inverter fault contribution at 1.2 × 1.8 MW = 2.16 MVA, or about 100 A at 12.47 kV, but that estimate is not taken from Bramwick inverter data (there is no application record) and cannot establish that any particular device remains below 87.5% of its interrupting rating or that a DPS-07 coordination margin holds. The DPS-07 §5.1(c) coordination study is required before energization, but it is a later deliverable, not a substitute for the screen.

Result: INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass. The study agreement scope must obtain the feeder device ratings and fault study, calculate the DER contribution at the POI, test each device against 87.5% of its interrupting rating, and test the DPS-07 coordination margins. Any device above 87.5% or margin below DPS-07 is a screen failure and a study/upgrade item.

4.4 Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load

Screen D PASSES: the requested 1,800 kW is below the 2,400 kW daytime-window minimum by 600 kW (25.0%). The full calculation, data-quality review and exclusions are in §5. The pass depends on the requested capacity being 1,800 kW; that figure is the v1-stated request and has not been verified against a filed application because no application record is on file. If the as-filed AC nameplate differs, Screen D must be rerun.

4.5 Screen E — reverse power at the substation

SRP-3 Screen E has two independent triggers: (a) aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the substation transformer’s certified reverse-power capability; or (b) reverse-power protective settings are not in place. Either trigger routes the application to study.

What the record shows. No Larkspur Ridge transformer certified reverse-power capability is stated anywhere in the records before 07/14/2025, and no reverse-power settings are in the record. The memo cannot test either trigger. A comparison of the 1,800 kW request with the ALN-214 load minimum is not the capability test. The transformer aggregate is also incomplete: HCM-2024-Q2 shows both ALN-205 and ALN-214 at Larkspur Ridge, and the 07/14/2025 active queue contains seven ALN-205 rows with filed capacity totalling 9.23 MW, including Brackenhaven Community Solar at 1.8 MW (PXA-2024-0077, system impact study SIS-2025-023). The ALN-214-only 1,800 kW figure does not establish the transformer’s exposure.

Correction to the earlier v2 draft. At night the Bramwick solar facility is not generating; its output is 0 kW, not 1,800 kW. The 1,985 kW reading at 2025-01-19 07:30 is a load minimum before solar production, not a night-time comparison with 1,800 kW of generation. The earlier statement that the night aggregate “remains 1,800 kW” was physically wrong and is corrected here. The correction does not change the Screen E result, which is inconclusive for want of capability and settings.

Result: INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass. The study agreement scope must obtain the transformer nameplate and certified reverse-power capability, the reverse-power settings, and a complete aggregate of all DER on both Larkspur Ridge feeders; it must confirm the feeder assignment of Larkspur Warehouse PV, 550 kW. If the aggregate exceeds the capability, or the settings are not in place, Screen E is a study item in any event.

5. Screen D calculation and data review

5.1 Method required by SRP-3 Rev 3 §4

The screen uses the minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent complete twelve calendar months, at 15-minute intervals aligned to the feeder collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within the window. The absolute overnight minimum must not be used. Requested DER capacity must be less than or equal to that daytime minimum. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers or planned switching must be excluded and documented.

5.2 Data window and interval count

Table 5-1 — AMI data set


5.3 Minimum-load results

Table 5-2 — Screen D minimum-load results


The lowest ten daytime-window readings are listed in Appendix A. The next reading after 2,400 kW is 2,418 kW; the Screen D result does not depend on the single 2,400 kW point.

5.4 Data quality and exclusions

No ALN-214 feeder outage, load transfer or planned-switching record was found in the DER Program records as of 07/14/2025. No interval was therefore excluded on those grounds, and the memo records that fact as required by SRP-3 §4 and §6(c).

Two single-interval downward excursions were identified by comparing each reading with the median of its neighbouring intervals:

2025-03-23 03:45 — 1,100 kW, bracketed by 3,882 kW at 03:30 and 3,568 kW at 04:00. This is outside the daytime window and is the only 1.1 MW reading in the file. It is an isolated transient, not a sustained overnight minimum. It is not used for Screen D. Excluding it, the absolute minimum is 1,985 kW at 2025-01-19 07:30.

2025-02-12 11:30 — 2,400 kW, bracketed by 3,575 kW at 11:15 and 3,689 kW at 11:45. This is inside the daytime window and is the lowest daytime reading. It is retained in the Screen D calculation to keep the result conservative. If it were excluded as an abnormal interval, the daytime minimum would be 2,418 kW at 2025-01-25 10:00, which only increases the pass margin.

The v1 memo’s 1.1 MW figure matches the first of these single-interval excursions. It is not a valid Screen D basis: it is outside 10:00–16:00 and SRP-3 §4 expressly prohibits using the absolute overnight minimum.

5.5 Comparison and result

Table 5-3 — Screen D comparison


Screen D passes with 600 kW (25.0%) of margin on the conservative raw minimum, or 618 kW (25.6%) using the clean 2,418 kW value. The request is not at the limit, so rounding, a different interval within the window, or a stricter reading of the clause does not change the result. If the Larkspur Warehouse PV (550 kW) were confirmed on ALN-214, the identified aggregate would be 2,350 kW, still 50 kW (2.1%) below the daytime minimum; that is an aggregate sensitivity for Screens A and E, not a change to the Screen D comparison, but it leaves little reserve and any later addition on ALN-214 must be re-screened.

6. Reconciliation with the 06/25/2025 memo (v1)

The v1 memo does not stand. Its Screen D conclusion rests on a minimum-load figure that the procedure does not permit and on a data window and cadence that do not match the AMI file on record. Table 6-1 lists each discrepancy.

Table 6-1 — v1 reconciliation


The v1 arithmetic (1.8 MW > 1.1 MW) is correct; its input and method are not. The error is one of basis, not of comparison: v1 used the absolute overnight minimum that SRP-3 §4 expressly says must not be used, and it treated a single 15-minute transient as the feeder minimum. The v1 Screen D failure is withdrawn. The v1 recommendation of a Study Agreement is not adopted on its reasoning — that reasoning depends on the failed Screen D. The final disposition is still a study agreement, but for the different and independent reasons in §4: Screens A, B, C and E are inconclusive, and the application record is incomplete. The fact that both memos reach a study outcome does not validate v1.

7. Disposition and required actions

Disposition: ADVANCE TO STUDY AGREEMENT. SRP-3 Rev 3 §2 is explicit: where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record, the application shall be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed. Screens A, B, C and E are inconclusive; Screen D passes. The Screen D pass cannot carry the application. DIS-01 Table 3-1 independently specifies a system impact study for a medium-scale facility, and the DIS-01/SRP-3 conflict is referred under ERP-9; both paths lead to study on this record. This disposition does not authorize interconnection, construction, energization or Permission to Operate; those remain subject to the balance of DIS-01, DPS-07 and TCS-02.

Application-record deficiency and return to the applicant. The file contains no complete application and no PXA/queue number. Tariff §12.3 requires an application determined incomplete to be returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which cure is required. The file is therefore returned to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC with that notice. The study agreement is not to be executed until the complete application, PXA and queue position are on record. This is not a “return without study”: the study agreement is the required disposition once the record is complete, and the study scope in Table 7-1 is to be ready to issue on cure.

Table 7-1 — Required actions


8. Scope, assumptions and limitations

Scope. This memo determines the SRP-3 Rev 3 supplemental review for Bramwick Commons Solar on Feeder ALN-214 as of 07/14/2025. It supersedes the 06/25/2025 v1 memo. It does not decide a system impact study, a protection coordination study, a witness-test disposition, a telemetry design, an ISA, construction approval, energization or PTO. The study agreement required by this memo is the next procedural step; the engineering studies remain to be performed.

## Bottom line

The v1 Screen D failure does not stand: the correct daytime minimum is 2,400 kW and the 1,800 kW request passes Screen D with 600 kW of margin. But the memo's further conclusion — that all of Screens A–E pass and the application advances without a study agreement — is **not supported by the record**. Screens A, B, C and E are inconclusive on the documents the memo itself says are missing; the application has no PXA/queue record; and DIS-01 Table 3-1's medium-scale review path is a system impact study. On the standard 15%-of-peak fast-track screen, Screen A would fail (1,800 kW is 21.1% of the 8,526 kW peak), so the Screen A pass is not merely unsupported but potentially contrary to the applicable penetration limit. Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §2 the disposition must be **advance to a study agreement** (or, if the application record cannot be produced, **return to the applicant with the specified deficiency**; in either case the missing records must be obtained and the screens re-run before a no-study disposition is issued).

# Bramwick Commons Screening Memo v1

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW SCREEN DETERMINATION
To:      Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
From:   Priya Ranganathan, Interconnection Studies
Date:   06/25/2025
Subject: Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW, Feeder ALN-214) — Supplemental Review Screen Determination
1. Project
The application was routed to supplemental review following failure of an initial fast-track screen. This memo records the disposition of the 100%-of-minimum-load screen applied under SRP-3 Rev 3.
2. Screen applied
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar, per §4 of SRP-3 (Rev 3, effective 02/10/2025). Under this screen, the requested DER capacity is compared against the minimum load observed on the subject feeder from AMI interval data.
3. Analysis
Reviewed AMI interval load data for Feeder ALN-214 from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse and identified a minimum feeder load of 1.1 MW. The value was drawn from the feeder AMI record available on file for ALN-214. No intervals were excluded for known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching during the period reviewed.
4. Comparison
1.8 MW requested exceeds 1.1 MW minimum feeder load — screen FAILED.
5. Recommendation
Study Agreement required prior to advancement. The application should not proceed on the supplemental-review track. A Study Agreement should be offered to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC, with the scope covering the technical conditions that gave rise to the failed screen on Feeder ALN-214.
6. Disposition
Return supplemental review file to Interconnection Studies queue with a failed-screen flag on Feeder ALN-214.
Notify the applicant of the screen result and forward the Study Agreement package.
Hold advancement of PXA record for Bramwick Commons Solar until Study Agreement is executed.
